entries.name: Cherry Bloom
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to burst a cherry bloom on hit
entries.notes: SHIPPED — id, kind and op kept verbatim: naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies g.board existingFamilies lists cherry_bloom, and AtomKindRegistry's board.action schema (src/FusionRpg.Core/Effects/Atoms/AtomKindRegistry.cs) states 'Ops are freeze|doom|fireline|cherry' — op:cherry is this family's own opcode, not a free choice. `damage` is the schema's Value param and is OMITTED per seed-contract.md §3: the generator supplies it from `powerBand`, exactly the way `amount` is absent from the exemplar's elemental_power. No `row`/`col` — those are for a fixed-cell debug cast, not a proc that must resolve its cell from the trigger's own event. `when: OnDamageDealt` reads as a Cherry-Bomb-style burst riding the wearer's own hit, the same shape as g.on-hit's searing_strike.

entries.name: Dooming
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to detonate the board on death
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id/kind/op kept verbatim (op:doom is one of board.action's four fixed ops). The biggest single blast in the shipped op set (Doom-shroom's crater), so it carries this partition's only `extreme` band — a relative-pull judgement against its siblings, same convention the exemplar uses between elemental_power and elpw-amplify. `when: OnDeath` reads as the wearer detonating the board on its own death, the same trigger deathblast (g.on-death) already uses for its damage burst.

entries.name: Firelining
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to lay a line of fire on hit
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id/kind/op kept verbatim (op:fireline). A sustained lane-wide burn rather than one burst, so it sits at `medium` between cherry-bloom's single detonation and dooming's whole-board nuke. `when: OnDamageDealt` matches the on-hit shape of the other proc-style board ops in this group.

entries.name: Flash Freeze
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to flash-freeze the attacker when struck
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id/kind/op kept verbatim (op:freeze). Distinct wordset from g.affliction's own `freezing` status.apply family (of Chill/of Rime/of the Glacier, ssot-affixes.md line 755) — same idea, different mechanism and different group, so a shared word would be a real, not cosmetic, collision. Given a defensive trigger (`OnDamageTaken`) rather than the offensive on-hit shape of this group's other three board.action families, so it is control rather than damage and tagged `utility`, not `offensive` — no `control` value exists on tags.v1.json's combat-posture axis, and `utility` is the closer of the two remaining ones for a pure crowd-control proc. `low` band reflects that its value is the disable, not a magnitude.

entries.name: Gravemaking
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to raise a grave where the target falls
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id/kind kept verbatim; word table reused verbatim from ssot-affixes.md line 758 (already shown shipped there). `gridItemType: "Grave"` is the readable enum word, not the raw int the ParamDef declares (`ParamKind.Int`, AtomKindRegistry.cs) — the same author-a-word/generator-resolves-the-int convention ssot-uniques.md §... already uses for box.set's boxType (`boxType: Lava (Int per D7)`), and matches the overlay-level examples in effect-data.md (`{"gridItemType":"Grave"}`). No registry enumerates the legal words today, which is a real gap (parallel to entry-shapes.md's material-runtimeId finding), but `Grave` is the only value that makes this family's own name true, so it is not a guess. `graveType` (also on the schema) is omitted: AtomKindRegistry's own ParamDef note says 'the sink does not forward graveType' — authoring it would lie about what fires. `when: OnDeath` reads as a grave forming where the wearer's kill falls.

entries.name: Gravedigging
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to clear a nearby grave when struck
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id/kind kept verbatim; new word table minted (ssot-affixes.md's illustrative sample shows one for the sibling `gravemaking` only). `gridItemType: "Grave"` again names the readable enum word rather than the ParamDef's raw int, same convention and same caveat as gravemaking's entry. `selector` (also on grid.clear's schema, `ParamKind.String`) is omitted — no registry names its legal values, and inventing one would be exactly the guess seed-contract.md's BLOCKED path exists to avoid for a field this narrow. Given `OnDamageTaken` rather than gravemaking's `OnDeath`, this reads as the defensive mirror of its sibling: clearing a grave near you when you are struck, rather than leaving one where a kill falls.

entries.name: Terraforming
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to scorch the ground to lava on hit
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id/kind kept verbatim; word table reused verbatim from ssot-affixes.md line 759 (already shown shipped there). atom-family-library.md §3.5 describes this family's LIVE-proven range as 'Water / Grass / Lava / Dirt', all four box types, but box.set's ParamDef takes exactly one `boxType` per atom row (G2: the executor also only ever handles one cell, never `cells[]`) and no registry or generator directive expands a family across box-type variants the way `variants: {generate: "elements+omni"}` does for elements. Rather than invent an unowned expansion mechanism, this entry authors the single most load-bearing type — `Lava`, the one that itself deals ongoing damage, matching the precedent already set in ssot-uniques.md's own worked example (`box.set`, `boxType: Lava (Int per D7)`). `boxType: "Lava"` is the readable word, not the raw int `ParamKind.Int` declares; see the gravemaking entry's note on the same convention. Tagged `utility` per atom-family-library.md's own Cat mark ('U') for this family, even though the effect it sets is itself damaging terrain.
